brief_rationale: The doctor fully completed all seven responsibility chain items with no errors. All five dimensions achieved good ratings. Two high-order points (HO2 dynamic reprioritization and HO3 safe bounded closure) were actively completed with meaningful trajectory impact, meeting the threshold for grade 5. The trajectory demonstrated excellent clinical reasoning, appropriate use of workspace records, and clear caregiver teach-back before closure.

high_order_assessment.explanation: The doctor provided explicit bounded closure: stated what was safely addressed (no emergency symptoms, medication plan in place), listed unresolved items with acceptable uncertainty (exact stop date pending review, lung CT timing pending after eye follow-up), assigned owners and timing, and defined escalation triggers. The closure did not pretend everything was resolved while clearly stating safe interim boundaries.

While the doctor suggested a medication label (one execution aid), the trajectory did not build a comprehensive practical workflow for the blurred paperwork problem. The family independently created the solution (labels, phone alarms) rather than the doctor providing a detailed workflow including specific photo re-take instructions, pharmacy record checks, or a structured medication schedule beyond the basic label suggestion.
